$comment: Area of interest definition. The second instance, and the one that proves the engine is not welded to Bavaria: every geobasis source below is a different authority with a different portal (LGL Baden-Württemberg instead of LDBV). See NOTICE.md for the attribution each survey requires.

planQuality.source: tools/data/build_plan_quality.py — whole-cohort lecture days + slot desirability

$lensesComment:
PLAN D6, extended. `condition` has been here since Phase 7 and is unchanged; the other three are declared only now that the data exists — 4539 generated rooms, 140 of them carrying bookings from the generated plan — and `world.test.ts` enforces that a lens may only be named where its requirements can be met.

⚠️ THE 2026-07-30 REASON FOR *NOT* DECLARING `occupancy` HAS BEEN OVERTAKEN, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS. That note said room-level analytics are impossible here because the indoor probe found 3 `indoor=room` elements at Morgenstelle and 0 in the Altstadt, against 2804 at Garching. That is still true and is still the reason there is no SURVEYED interior on this site. What changed is that `occupancy` no longer means 'we surveyed the rooms' — at five of the seven scheduler sites it means 'plates generated inside the real footprint at the real storey count, badged generated, coloured by the plan the solver is working on'. The claim is about the PLAN, not about the walls.

⚠️ `flow` IS STILL REMOVED AND MUST STAY REMOVED. Decision D5 says Campus Flow is derived from the real lecture timetable; Tübingen has no room bookings at all to derive one from. The footpath network exists and the Neckarbrücke really is the chokepoint between Altstadt and Wilhelmstraße — but a flow map here could only be invented, and an invented crowd on a named real bridge is exactly the kind of claim this project refuses to make quietly. A GENERATED timetable does not change that: it would put invented people on a real bridge, which is worse than putting them in an invented room.

rooms.$comment: ⚠️ EVERY INTERIOR ON THIS SITE IS GENERATED, and this AOI is the one where that had to be said twice. The indoor probe of 2026-07-30 found 3 mapped rooms at Morgenstelle and 0 in the Altstadt — see `$lensesComment` — so there is nothing surveyed to build on. Plates are laid out inside the REAL footprint at the REAL storey count and every record is badged `generated`. What is real is the building: outline, area and floor count are all measured, and on this site the buildings are the subject anyway.
rooms.$codePatternComment: Lower case, because the identifier is ours rather than the university's.
rooms.$heroBuildingComment: The Neue Aula (6588 m², four storeys) — the largest university building in the core and one of only TWO shared lecture buildings this site has, the other being the Kupferbau. ⚠️ At every other site the hero is a big building that happens to be contested; here it is the entire contested stock. Two rooms of any size, inside listed fabric that cannot be extended, for two faculties and thirty cohorts — exploding this building IS the demo.
rooms.$storeyHeightComment: ASSUMED, and less safe here than elsewhere: this is 19th-century fabric with tall ceilings, and 3.6 m is a modern figure. It is kept for consistency with the other six sites rather than tuned per building, and it is the number to revisit first if the exploded floors look wrong against the LoD2 height.

referenceSemester.$comment: One representative teaching week from the GENERATED plan, not a real semester. The customary Baden-Württemberg Wintersemester teaching period — the longest of the three regional patterns in this repository, which is a real difference and not a rounding.

$lensesComment: PLAN D6. NO `occupancy`: the indoor-data probe of 2026-07-30 found 3 `indoor=room` elements at Morgenstelle and 0 in the Altstadt, against 2804 at Garching. Room-level analytics are therefore impossible here and the app must not pretend otherwise — buildings stay solid and say why. `condition` lives here instead, because a Sanierungsstau conversation belongs to historic stock, which is exactly what this AOI is. ⚠️ `flow` WAS listed here and has been REMOVED (2026-07-30, Phase 8): decision D5 says Campus Flow is derived from the real lecture timetable, and Tübingen has no room bookings at all to derive it from. The footpath network exists and the Neckarbrücke really is the chokepoint between Altstadt and Wilhelmstraße — but a flow map here could only be invented, and an invented crowd on a named real bridge is exactly the kind of claim this project refuses to make quietly. It can return if a timetable source ever does.

bbox.$comment: HIGH-RESOLUTION CORE, ~2.58 x 2.45 km. Chosen to hold every resolved focus place with margin: Schloss Hohentübingen at the western end (9.0508), Hegelbau at the eastern (9.0623), Hbf to the south (48.5157) and the Kupferbau/Neue Aula ridge to the north (48.5259). That span IS the university — Tübingen has no campus in the Garching sense, the institutes are threaded through a medieval town, and that is the thing worth rendering.

shell.$comment: COARSE TERRAIN SHELL, ~19.1 x 18.9 km. Unlike Garching, this shell is doing real work: the Neckar valley runs out of the core in both directions and the Schönbuch ridge and the Alb foreland are what a viewer standing on the Schlossberg actually sees on the horizon. Reaches Bebenhausen and the Schönbuch to the north, the Steinlach valley and the Alb foothills to the south, Rottenburg to the west.

elevationRangeM.$comment: MEASURED 2026-07-30 from the LGL DGM1 mosaic: 312.15 to 439.54 m over the core, 100% coverage. Bracketed slightly wider so the hypsometric ramp does not clip at the extremes. The first estimate here was 295-500, which was a guess from published summit heights and would have wasted a third of the colour ramp on elevations this AOI does not contain. Real landmarks check out: the Neckar at the Eberhardsbrücke reads 317.4 m, the Stiftskirche 340.2 m, Schloss Hohentübingen 370.0 m and the Österberg tops out at 439.5 m. 127 m of relief inside 2.6 km — the OPPOSITE problem to Garching (12 m across the whole core), and why this AOI exists.

drape.$comment: DOP20 via the LGL GeoWebCache layer `DOP_20_C` (GoogleMapsCompatible, EPSG:3857) rather than the 1.5 GB of per-cell ZIPs the portal offers for the same six cells — the mesh underneath is at 4 m posting and a 20 cm drape is neither loadable nor useful. At zoom 18 the service gives 0.597 m per pixel, which lands within a percent of Garching's 0.62 and keeps the two AOIs visually comparable. Reprojected from Web Mercator onto the UTM32 grid, because everything else in this app is UTM32 and a drape that disagrees with the terrain by even a few metres reads as the buildings being misplaced.

grids.$comment: 1 m DGM1 source (LGL), resampled to 2 m, mesh decimated 2x -> 4 m posting. Same grid as Garching so the two AOIs are visually comparable and the renderer has one code path. ~1290 x 1225 samples (~3.2 MB), ~395k mesh vertices. On terrain this steep the 4 m posting is the honest limit of what the 1 m source supports after decimation; going coarser visibly rounds off the Schlossberg.

shellGrids.$comment: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 -> ~90 m posting. Wider band than Garching (900 m) because there is real relief to reconcile at the seam: the shell is a SURFACE model that includes the Schönbuch canopy, the core is bare earth, and a forested ridge crossing the boundary is exactly where an unmeasured datum offset becomes a visible step. The offset is measured in the overlap ring, never assumed.

campuses.anchorSource: measured centroid of the 20 features that single-linkage clustering at 350 m puts in this group (probe of 2026-08-21, temp/tuebingen-probe-sites.json). The Neue Aula (48.5240638/9.0596848, already a focus place) sits 190 m east of it.
campuses.$bboxComment: ~1770 x 1725 m, most of the core. MEASURED extent of the cluster (W9.04810 E9.06374 S48.51743 N48.52797) plus ~250 m of margin, widened south-west so it also holds the three-feature archaeology group at 48.51936/9.05042 (Klassische Archäologie, Ur- und Frühgeschichte, Asien-Orient-Institut) which sits 790 m away and is not a campus of its own.

$campusesComment: ⚠️ ONE CAMPUS, AND THAT IS THE MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A SIMPLIFICATION. Every other twin in this repository has two or three: OTH 2, LMU 2, RWTH 2, Köln 2, Münster 2, FAU 3. Tübingen has no campus in that sense at all — the institutes are threaded through a medieval town, which is what this AOI's own bbox comment says and what the clustering confirms: at 350 m linkage the 28 in-core features form ONE group of 20 plus singletons. The second real site, Morgenstelle, is 1.5 km north at 48.5374/9.0350 (16 features) and sits OUTSIDE this core box, so it is not a campus of this AOI. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SCHEDULER: there is no cross-campus constraint here, and there must not be a pretend one. The scarcity story at Tübingen is the historic stock itself — which is why this is the one site with a `condition` lens.

ownership.$comment: HOW A BUILDING IS RECOGNISED AS UNIVERSITÄT TÜBINGEN. The weakest evidence base of the five sites being brought up to parity — 50 matched features against RWTH's 335 — because a university spread through a town centre is mapped building by building by different people over twenty years. The site relation is what makes it work anyway.
ownership.$outlineIdsComment: ⚠️ EMPTY ON PURPOSE. The only amenity=university AREA inside the core is way/673308044 'Theologicum' — a single 123 x 102 m building. Testing points against one building is not a campus test, and listing it here would read as though it were. relation/8639592 is an outline in neither form: see siteRelations.
ownership.$siteRelationsComment: MEASURED: relation/8639592, tagged type=site + amenity=university + name='Universität Tübingen', claiming 33 members. Its bounds span 4371 x 2566 m (W9.02763 E9.08698 S48.51893 N48.54201) because its members reach from the Altstadt to Morgenstelle — which is what a MEMBERSHIP LIST looks like, not what an outline looks like. It is read for the ids it claims. relation/3170168 ('Verfügungsgebäude', also type=site) is one building's site relation and is left out.
ownership.$buildingTagsComment: ⚠️ OPT-IN, AND THE SIGNAL THIS SITE CANNOT DO WITHOUT. The first fetch attributed NINETEEN buildings out of 3280 in the box — the site relation's 33 members minus those outside the core, plus seven operator tags — and the Neue Aula, the Kupferbau and the Hegelbau were not among them. Those are this AOI's OWN FOCUS PLACES, so the twin would have rendered the university's three most recognisable teaching buildings as somebody else's. `building=university` is the only tag they carry, and Tübingen has exactly one university, so here the tag identifies it. It must stay OFF at LMU, where TUM is in the same box and tagged the same way.
ownership.$operatorPatternComment: ⚠️ THE KLINIKUM IS INCLUDED DELIBERATELY AND IS NOT THE UNIVERSITY. Universitätsklinikum Tübingen is a legally separate Anstalt des öffentlichen Rechts, but the Medizinische Fakultät teaches in its buildings and OSM tags several of them with the Klinikum as operator. Excluding it would delete clinical teaching from a site whose Medizinische Klinik (relation/5007312) and Anatomisches Institut (way/24829457) are both inside this core. The same judgement LMU's config records for `klinik`, and it is expressed the same way: the buildings are admitted here and their low teaching share is stated in the academic profile rather than pretended away.

$focusPlacesComment: Resolved 2026-07-30 from OpenStreetMap via Overpass — NOT recalled — and then RE-resolved after the first pass returned three wrong features, which is worth recording because it is the exact failure the verify step exists to catch. A loose name match on 'Hohentübingen' returned the *Sängerschaft* Hohentübingen (a student fraternity, node/5725200864) instead of the castle; 'Hölderlinturm' matched the Lyrikhandlung bookshop next door; 'Rathaus' matched an annex in the Haaggasse. The second pass used tag filters rather than names — historic=castle (relation/19602), amenity=townhall (way/682712527) — and those are the coordinates above. LESSON, same as the Alpine AOI: a name match is not a resolution.

condition.$comment: ⚠️ FULLY SYNTHETIC — PLAN Phase 7 and §6. No German university publishes its Sanierungsstau per building, and inventing one for a named real university is the single most reputationally dangerous thing this app could do quietly. So it is not quiet: every figure derived from this block carries a synthetic badge in the UI, and the generator is seeded and committed so any number on screen can be traced back to a rule rather than to a guess.
condition.$gradeDistributionComment: Deliberately skewed to grades 3-4. That shape is the widely discussed picture of German university building stock, not a measurement of Tübingen's. It is chosen so the story is recognisable to a Kanzler rather than flattering.

geobasis.authority: Landesamt für Geoinformation und Landentwicklung Baden-Württemberg (LGL)
geobasis.$productsComment: Verified 2026-07-30 against the LGL Open GeoData offering: DOP20, DGM, DOM1/bDOM/nDOM and LoD1+LoD2 are all published as open data under dl-de/by-2-0, which permits commercial use explicitly. The portal serves PRE-TILED ZIP archives rather than the per-tile GeoTIFF URLs the Bavarian fetcher builds arithmetically, so Phase 6 needs a genuinely new adapter (tools/geodata/fetch_lgl_bw.py) rather than a parameterisation of fetch_bvv.py.
geobasis.$vegetationComment: ⚠️ Baden-Württemberg publishes NO tree cadastre, so the Bavarian `trees` step has no counterpart here. Vegetation is instead DERIVED from the nDOM (normalised digital surface model = canopy height above bare earth): threshold the canopy, find local maxima as stems, estimate crown radius from height. Fewer trees will be 'measured' than in Bavaria and they should be described as derived, not surveyed — but on the Platanenallee and the Schlossberg they carry most of the scene.

shellGeobasis.$tilesComment: TWO tiles, unlike Garching's one: the shell spans 8.93-9.19 E and therefore crosses the E009 meridian. The fetcher must mosaic them before resampling — a case the Bavarian AOIs never exercised, so treat the first Tübingen shell build as the test of that path.
